recall_prompt: Say how you would find n when n P 4 is 1680.
insider_note: Same method as ⁿP₃ = 1320 but with FOUR consecutive factors: 1680 = 8 · 7 · 6 · 5, so n = 8 — writing only three factors is the slip this version is built around.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write 1680 as four consecutive factors
steps.margin_note: First mark. ⁿP₄ is a product of 4 consecutive whole numbers counting down from n. 1680 = 8 · 7 · 6 · 5.

recall.must_convey: That n P 4 is the product of four consecutive numbers from n down, and 1680 is 8 times 7 times 6 times 5.
accept: n P four is n into n minus one into n minus two into n minus three and sixteen eighty is eight times seven times six times five
break sixteen eighty into four consecutive numbers eight seven six five
one thousand six hundred eighty is eight into seven into six into five
sixteen eighty ni eight seven six five ga rayali
four consecutive factors of sixteen eighty

steps.why: Solving n(n − 1)(n − 2)(n − 3) = 1680 as a polynomial is a quartic; matching it to a product of four consecutive numbers is the whole method.
common_mistakes: Writing only three factors n(n − 1)(n − 2) — ⁿP₄ has four.
Factoring 1680 as 10 · 8 · 7 · 3, which are not consecutive.

steps.label: Compare and state n

recall.must_convey: That comparing the two products gives n = 8.
accept: compare the products so n is eight
the largest factor is eight so n is eight

steps.why: The product of four consecutive numbers increases with n, so only one n fits, and it is the largest factor.
common_mistakes: Writing n = 8 without the comparison line.
